newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end higher, Dow snaps 3-day losing run.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end higher, Dow snaps 3-day losing run.

text.p: U.S. stocks rallied Thursday as the Dow Jones Industrial Average regained its bullish tone after three straight losing sessions.
The Dow added 58 points to close unofficially at 7777, a few points shy of its record high close of 7782 set last week. The blue-chip average knocked through 7800 in late trade before settling back.
Stocks got off to a strong start after a well-known market bull, Ralph Acampora of Prudential Securities, raised his target for the 30-issue Dow index to 10,000 in the next year.
The market was also given a boost by the approach of "triple-witching," the simultaneous expiration of futures and options on Friday, traders said.

"There's a lot of buying momentum out there. (Acampora) just keeps on increasing his numbers. That creates a very strong bullish feeling on Wall Street," said Warren Epstein, director of trading at Richard Rosenblatt

"Remain fully invested -- we expect the stock market to mount an explosive advance during the second half of the year," Acampora, Prudential Securities' director of technical research, said in a report.

Two government reports also set the bullish tone for the session. Initial claims for jobless benefits rose to 347,000 in the past week from 339,000, suggesting to analysts that the labor market might have cooled slightly. That ought to make the Federal Reserve feel more comfortable about keeping interest rates on hold at its July meeting.

The government also said the U.S. trade deficit rose 7.8 percent in April to $8.4 billion but noted that exports reached a record high. That could mean bigger profits ahead for U.S. companies doing business abroad, analysts said.
The market's upswing gained momentum ahead of Friday's "triple witching" expiration of futures and options, which tends to generate a sharper swings in share prices and higher volume, traders said.
To be sure, there was some unsettling economic news, with Philadelphia Federal Reserve's June business activity index jumping to 25.2, well above expectations of a 7.3 reading.
Afte the report, the Dow slipped off its early gains, as some players worried a strengthening economy might lead to a credit tightening.
But analysts chose to see the report as evidence that the economy was set for a robust third quarter without a rate hike. The long bond closed up 3/32 to yield 6.68 percent.

"When you see the market ignore bad news, that could mean something speculative is going on. It might be a clue the inflow to mutual funds is so big, there's a great sense of urgency for portfolio managers to buy," said Hugh Johnson, market analyst for First Albany.
Tobacco and drugs were strong, while oil and airline stocks fell.
Tobacco stocks rose as investors anticipated liability settlement talks could soon yield an agreement, traders said.

Philip Morris Cos Inc and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp were the most heavily traded stocks on the Big Board. Philip Morris closed up 2 to 47-1/2 after touching a 52-week high of 48-1/8 during the day. RJR rose 1-3/8 to 35-7/8.
Brown & Williamson's parent B.A.T Industries Plc, Lorillard Tobacco Co's parent Loews Corp and UST Inc also gained.
Airlines slid amid concern that tax proposals taking shape in Congress that could eat into the industry's profits. Goldman Sachs lowered its ratings on the three largest U.S. airlines.
AMR Corp slid 2 to 93-1/4, UAL Corp lost 2-3/8 to 71-7/8 and Delta Air Lines Inc fell 1 to 88-1/4.

The Nasdaq Composite closed to a record high, rising 14.71 to 1447.14 even though Microsoft Corp slipped. The shares lost 14/16 to 129-5/16 after Goldman Sachs said it expected the software company to meet Wall Street expectations for the fourth quarter, unlike the previous two quarters, when it handily beat the forecasts.
Among drug stocks, Merck and Co Inc rose 3-3/8 to 99-3/4, Johnson & Johnson tacked on 1-1/2 to 65-3/4 and Warner Lambert surged 6-7/8 to 112-3/4.
The S&P 500 rose 8.89 to 897.99, a record.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a two-to-one margin on the New York Stock Exchange. Volume was 536.9 million shares, according to the NYSE.
(Prices official as of 1645 EST/2045 GMT).
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
